problem.title: First and Last Visit Status Per Patient
problem.prompt: You are analyzing a telehealth visit funnel. Each patient may have multiple visit records as they progress from booking through provider sign-off. Write a query that returns one row per patient showing their patient_id, the status of their FIRST visit (earliest by scheduled_time), and the status of their LAST visit (latest by scheduled_time). A patient may have only one visit record, in which case first and last status will be identical. Order results by patient_id ascending. Use window functions to retrieve the first and last status values within each patient's visit history.

composite_moves: PARTITION BY patient_id ORDER BY scheduled_time
LAST_VALUE(status) OVER (... ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING)
DISTINCT to collapse partition rows to one row per patient

hints: You need to retrieve both the earliest and latest status value for each patient using window functions.
FIRST_VALUE and LAST_VALUE can be used with PARTITION BY patient_id ORDER BY scheduled_time, but be careful with the frame specification for LAST_VALUE.

The default frame for LAST_VALUE is RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW, which returns the current row's value, not the partition's last. Use ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING to get the true last value, then SELECT DISTINCT to return one row per patient.
problem.answer_key:
SELECT DISTINCT
  patient_id,
  FIRST_VALUE(status) OVER (PARTITION BY patient_id ORDER BY scheduled_time) AS first_status,
  LAST_VALUE(status) OVER (PARTITION BY patient_id ORDER BY scheduled_time ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS last_status
FROM telehealth_visits
ORDER BY patient_id;

_meta.scenario: a telehealth visit completion funnel from booking to provider sign-off

user_solution:
/* notes */

SELECT DISTINCT
    patient_id,
    FIRST_VALUE(status) OVER (PARTITION BY patient_id ORDER BY scheduled_time
                              ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS first_status,
    LAST_VALUE(status) OVER (PARTITION BY patient_id ORDER BY scheduled_time
                               ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS last_status
FROM telehealth_visits
ORDER BY patient_id;
